claims.text: Atomic-size-mismatch-induced lattice distortions predominantly govern strength and deformation behavior in multi-component concentrated alloys.
Atomic size differences among constituent elements generate local lattice distortions.
Lattice distortions create spatial fluctuations in the elastic field.
Spatial fluctuations in the elastic field impede dislocation glide.
Impeded dislocation glide increases the stress required to initiate plasticity.
Impeded dislocation glide enhances work hardening.
Alloys with greater atomic size mismatch will have higher yield strength than baseline alloys with minimal mismatch.
Alloys with greater atomic size mismatch will have higher work-hardening rates than baseline alloys with minimal mismatch.
Greater lattice distortion will produce observable dislocation configurations or dynamics consistent with increased obstruction.
The proposed relationship applies when the alloys are single-phase random solid solutions and deformation is dominated by dislocation–lattice interactions.
The proposed relationship is restricted to conditions where precipitation hardening and phase transformations are absent.
Composition can be varied to change atomic size mismatch while processing, grain size, and phase constitution are held constant.
Failure to observe higher strength, higher work-hardening rates, altered dislocation behavior, or a correlation between measured distortion and deformation resistance would falsify the hypothesis.
